reduceIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - UNCHANGED for the third consecutive session, and this time the level has EARNED it. The morning published 64,650, the midday held it verbatim against a session low that traded 130.8 points through it, and over the seven hours since, price never closed an hourly bar below 64,738. The line is now the single most tested number on this desk's board. What sits there: the daily EMA50 at 64,662.44 and the 1H EMA50 at 64,652.50 cluster within 10 points of each other, and directly beneath them is the 64,600-64,649 band where $72,565 of longs were force-sold this afternoon on top of the $190,915 the midday session documented. Spot is 64,876.9, so the line is 226.9 points below, 0.35%, comfortably inside a 2.18% daily ATR - it can be reached in a single thin overnight hour. It takes a CLOSE and not a touch because the level has now been wicked through once and defended; a wick here means nothing and a settled hourly bar means the daily EMA50 reclaim is void.

addIf.confirmation: A 4H CLOSE above $65,400 - also UNCHANGED from the midday report, and also deliberately. That trigger was set after 65,250 was poked at 65,388 and rejected with a 64,908.9 close, and the rule the midday session extracted from it - require a SETTLED bar, not a touch - is the best piece of process this desk has produced this week. Since then the session high is 65,100, 300 points short of the trigger, and the 4H closes have been 64,954.2 and 64,916.5 with the current bar at 64,885.9. Nothing has happened that justifies moving the line down toward price. Above 65,100 the next verified obstacle is the 65,050-65,099 shelf where $43,845 of shorts were bought back between 21:38 and 21:41Z, then the 65,388 high of 07 Aug.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from the midday REDUCE-on-weakness posture to a REDUCE that is actually EXECUTED, and the reason is portfolio shape rather than direction. The directional read has IMPROVED since midday - price is +161.5, the daily EMA50 at 64,662.44 has been reclaimed and held, the daily MACD histogram has tripled from +21.62 to +65.91, and 4H sits above all four of its EMAs. What has not improved is the wallet's exposure profile going into an unprotected Friday night: spot BTC is 85% of equity with 15% cash, and spot cannot carry a stop. Trimming a small slice of the core to rebuild cash is a defensive act, not a bearish one. Both trigger levels are UNCHANGED from midday - 64,650 reduce, 65,400 add - because both were correct and neither fired. The recommended stop moves from 64,500 to 64,480, below the 64,519.2 low and below the whole 64,500-64,549 liquidation shelf rather than sitting inside it.

overnightRisk: The gap to the next report is about 6h15m - this run stamps 19:50 COT Friday and the midnight session runs near 02:00 COT Saturday - but it is a FRIDAY NIGHT gap, and that is the specific problem. Five things make it dangerous. FIRST, liquidity has already left. The last liquidation of any kind on the OKX tape was at 21:41Z, three hours ago; 15m bar volume has collapsed from 60-100 BTC during the US session to 2.7-24 BTC in the last hour, and the 24h volume is 2,958 BTC. In a book that thin a single sizeable market order moves price 100+ points with nothing to absorb it, and the 64,821.8 low of the 23:45Z bar is a preview - it dropped 76 points on 44 BTC. SECOND, the ETF bid switches off. There are no creations or redemptions until Monday, so the four-day +763.6M inflow sequence that has underwritten this week's floor is simply absent for the whole weekend. Worse, today's Farside row is PROVISIONAL at +15.0M with IBIT still unreported - IBIT is the fund that has carried every positive day this month, and if it prints negative when the row completes, the 'five straight positive days' framing this report uses gets revised downward with no market open to react to it. THIRD, the Strait of Hormuz. Brent fell more than 7% over the week on Iran-Oman talks to restore shipping, but ADNOC reported attacks on three vessels transiting Hormuz and Iran is reportedly targeting vessels it deems hostile. A weekend escalation reprices oil, the dollar and every risk asset before any equity market can open, and BTC is the only one of them that trades through it. FOURTH, the payrolls repricing is twelve hours old and one-sided. Payrolls fell 23,000 against a consensus near +83,000; DXY dropped 0.5% to 99.60 near a two-month low and US10Y fell 7bp to 4.651. That move has not been stress-tested by a single Fed speaker. Weekend commentary that pushes back on the dovish read unwinds the dollar leg first and BTC second. FIFTH, and most concretely, the shelf below. $315,679 of REALIZED long liquidations sit stacked between 64,500 and 64,649 - 228 to 377 points under spot - and that is a proven high-volume transaction zone, not a guess. Thin books plus a proven shelf below is the exact configuration where an overnight air-pocket ends. A resting stop is the only protection that works while nobody is watching, and this report sets it at 64,480, BELOW that shelf and below the 64,519.2 low, rather than inside it.

In the 95 rows that postdate the midday 17:47 COT stamp, $317,468 of SHORTS were liquidated against $318,151 of LONGS - a 1.00-to-1.00 split, which is as close to perfectly two-sided as this feed ever prints. atr.source: Wilder ATR(14) on the OKX bar=1Dutc series, stated on the LAST COMPLETED daily bar (07 Aug UTC). The 07 Aug bar closed with high 65,388, low 64,159.6 and prior close 64,325.8, giving TR = 1,228.4 - the identical TR the midday session already incorporated while the bar was in progress, so the recursive value is unchanged at 1,417.01. pct = 1,417.01 / 64,876.9 = 2.18%. Cross-check for transparency: a direct 30-bar SMA-seeded Wilder computation over the same completed series gives 1,428.79, an 11.8-point difference from seeding. DELIBERATELY NOT USED: folding in the 47-minute-old 08 Aug in-progress bar, whose TR is only 131.3, would drag ATR to 1,325.17 - that is an artefact of a partial candle, not a contraction in volatility, and quoting it would understate overnight risk at exactly the wrong moment.

calibration.rollingRecord: 54 rows on file before this one. The midday session called range with a bearish tilt at 30/44/26 from 64,715.4, set position to REDUCE, held reduce at 64,650 and raised add to a 4H close above 65,400. Price is 64,876.9. Neither trigger fired and the direction was wrong: price went UP 161.5 points, +0.25%, over the seven hours. The levels were right, the tilt was not.
calibration.note: The midday row backfills to price_next_report 64,876.9, reduce_fired false, add_fired false, acting_helped FALSE. REDUCE did not fire - the lowest 1H CLOSE since the midday stamp is 64,738, and unlike the morning-to-midday window the level was not even wicked through this time, with the lowest trade at 64,661.3. ADD did not fire - the session high of 65,100 fell 300 points short of the required 4H close above 65,400. The recommended stop at 64,500 was NOT hit either, which retroactively validates the midday's own correction: it had widened the stop from the morning's 64,620 after that tighter level filled at 17:30Z, and the wider one survived a session low of 64,661.3 with 161 points to spare. THREE LESSONS TO CARRY. FIRST, the day's scoreboard is uncomfortable and worth stating flatly: four sessions, and the two that held their levels unchanged (midday, and now this one) were structurally right while the two that moved with price (morning lowering its add, midday tilting bearish after a red five hours) were directionally wrong. This desk's recurring error is not level selection - it is letting the last five hours of price action set the tilt. SECOND, the 'require a SETTLED bar' rule has now paid twice: it kept the desk out of the 65,388 false break, and it is the reason the add stays at 65,400 tonight rather than being lowered to 65,100. It is the single best process this desk has. THIRD, on stops - two sessions ago the placement was inside one hour's average range; the midday fixed it and the fix held. Tonight's 64,480 continues that discipline, sitting below the entire 64,500-64,649 liquidation shelf rather than inside it.
